vim behaviour: `:l` / `:list` print lines unambiguously (like `:set list`); with a range the cursor goes to the last line of it
m3 behaviour: `:l [NAME]` and `:list` open the generic list; a range is ignored; `:set list` is the way to see tabs and line ends
reason: the list is the one place results go (docs/LIST.md); the print variant has no use in a visual editor

m3 behaviour: `:g/pat/l` opens the generic list once per match
one list store of named lists; `:lnext` `:lprev` `:lfirst` `:llast` `:lclear` work on it; `:lopen` `:lwindow` `:lolder` do not exist
reason: a second store would hold nothing the first cannot (docs/LIST.md)

vim behaviour: nvim 0.11 maps `[q ]q [Q ]Q` to quickfix prev / next / first / last
m3 behaviour: not mapped; `[l ]l [L ]L` walk the default list
reason: the quickfix list is the generic list now; keys are not in the oracle corpus

vim behaviour: vi's `Q` enters Ex mode (vim), nvim 0.11 replays the last macro
reason: Vim commands behave like nvim (owner rule)

m3 behaviour: the hunk family `ghs ghr ghS ghR ghd ghD ghb ghl` (0.31.0); `gH` is refused
reason: m3 has no Select mode; the `gh` prefix serves staging, resetting, diffing and blaming hunks

m3 behaviour: CTRL-R redoes (as Vim and nvim do); CTRL-L redraws

vim behaviour: vi has 'remap'; nvim has no such option

reason: nvim has no open mode either

m3 behaviour: refused: `E492: Not an editor command: g? (rot13 is gone; ...)`
reason: an operator for a cipher; filter with `!{motion}tr` if needed (docs/DIVERGENCE-AUDIT.md)

m3 behaviour: refused: `gR (Virtual Replace is gone; use R)`
reason: the engine pretended (handled like Replace); only tabs differ

vim behaviour: `:a[ppend]` `:i[nsert]` `:c[hange]` read text lines up to a lone `.`
m3 behaviour: refused: `E492 ... type o, O or cc in Normal mode`
reason: script-only; m3 has no headless mode

vim behaviour: `:z` prints a page of lines and moves the cursor
'wrapmargin' breaks lines before the window edge
reason: depends on the window width; 'textwidth' is the tool

m3 behaviour: refused with the name of the generic-list or argument-list command to write instead
reason: one list API (docs/LIST.md); no corpus case uses them

vim behaviour: about 170 options are accepted and stored although nothing reads them
reason: a `:set` that does nothing hides that it does nothing; the reasons are in engine/MED_removed.m31

m3 behaviour: not built; `gQ` and `:visual` are refused, `-e` / `-E` are refused by the command line
reason: the command line `:` is the Ex line
new windows open below and right, what nearly everyone sets; the window oracle runs nvim with both on

vim behaviour: 'clipboard' is empty: the unnamed register is internal
m3 behaviour: 'clipboard' is `unnamedplus`: yanks and deletes also go to the system clipboard (or OSC 52), and `p` reads it
reason: yy and p should work across programs; the oracle has no clipboard provider, so its cases cannot see it
